rule_context:
FTC Endorsement Disclosure Policy

All influencer content where Vantage CPG or any of our brands provides compensation, free product, affiliate commissions, or any other material consideration must carry clear and conspicuous disclosure of the paid relationship. This applies regardless of platform native tools and regardless of whether the talent considers the relationship obvious from context.

The compliance standard is not platform labels alone. A post is in scope if three elements are present: (1) a material connection between talent and Vantage CPG or our brands, (2) an endorsement, recommendation, or product feature, and (3) dissemination to an audience that may not know of the connection. Where all three are present, disclosure must be unavoidable to the viewer, not buried in bios, hashtag blocks, or parentheticals at the end of copy.

Acceptable disclosure formats: paid partnership hashtag placed within the first three lines of visible caption text; audio disclosure in video content spoken by talent and displayed as on-screen text for the full duration; or platform-native paid partnership labels that are visible by default and not hidden behind expansion controls.

Unacceptable and non-compliant: disclosure only in bio, only at end of caption, only via affiliate code without accompanying text, only through platform tools without hashtag or audio reinforcement where platform tools are known to be inconsistently displayed, or any format the talent team describes as subtle or authenticity-focused that reduces viewer recognition of the paid relationship.

Brand managers are responsible for confirming disclosure placement before content goes live. Talent preference or authenticity concerns do not override this requirement. Legal holds final authority on what constitutes clear and conspicuous disclosure in emerging formats.
